meta.title: Leo's Octopus Cartoon
meta.textType: story: the main idea of a picture story

paragraphs: The Explorers visited a small aquarium on Saturday morning. Teacher Kim came with the class. Mia took photos of the fish, and Lily wrote notes for the blog. Leo took a notebook for his cartoons.

In the last room, there was a big tank with an octopus. It was orange, and it had eight long arms. At first, the octopus hid behind a gray stone. Then it came to the glass and looked at Leo. "It has big eyes," said Leo. "The woman at the door told me about it," said Mia. "It comes from the ocean. It is a wild animal." Leo looked at the octopus for a long time. "I have an idea," he said. "I will draw a cartoon with six pictures."

First, Leo drew the octopus in space. It sat in a small rocket and waved. In the next picture, the octopus threw a snowball at the moon. Leo laughed and showed the pictures to Mia. "No, no," said Mia. "An octopus does not live in space." "And it does not play with snow," said Lily. Leo thought for a minute. "You are right," he said. "The octopus wants to go home."

This was Leo's new cartoon. In picture one, the octopus was alone in the tank and looked at the door. In picture two, it climbed out and went across the floor. In picture three, it found a small stream behind the aquarium. In picture four, it followed the stream to the ocean. In picture five, many fish said hello to it. In picture six, the octopus sat on a stone in the blue water and smiled.

Teacher Kim read the cartoon first. "Where does the octopus go?" she asked. "It goes home to the ocean," said Lily. "We can see it in the pictures." "That is a good picture story," said Teacher Kim. Lily put the cartoon on Explorers' Blog that evening. Under it, Leo wrote, "Every wild animal has a home."
text.summary: The Explorers visit a small aquarium. Leo sees an octopus and draws a cartoon with six pictures, and the cartoon shows that the octopus wants to go home to the ocean.
